learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of container queries.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on container queries and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Container Queries helps you build layouts that remain consistent as content, viewport width and component context change.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Understanding element-based responsiveness; Creating query containers; Styling based on container dimensions; Using container query variants; Differences between viewport and container queries. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to container queries, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Complete the linked practical exercise “Container-aware product cards”. Build a reusable card that stacks at narrow container widths and changes to a row as its container grows.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to container queries.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to container queries.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: The card stacks content in narrow containers and changes to a row when its container reaches the configured breakpoint.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying container queries without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Container Queries is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
